sections.h2: The Grove Home Prices and Market Pace
sections.html:
In the 24 months from November 15, 2024 to November 14, 2026, 74 residential sales closed in The Grove (Chesapeake, VA) according to REIN MLS records. The median sold price was $419,900, close to the citywide median of $420,000, and homes took a median of 28 days to sell, slower than the citywide median of 18 days. These figures come from closed sales, which show what homes actually sold for rather than asking prices.

The middle half of The Grove sales closed between $386,400 and $436,650, or about $216 per square foot against $219 citywide. Split by year, the median sold price in the most recent 12 months ($427,900, 41 sales) was about 4% higher than in the earlier 12 months ($413,400, 33 sales). The typical home sold right at its list price (median sale-to-list ratio of 100%).

sections.h2: What Kinds of Homes Sell in The Grove
sections.html:
1% of the sales were detached homes and 99% were attached homes (townhomes or condos). The median home was about 2,044 square feet, with the middle half of sales running from roughly 1,642 to 2,044 square feet. 99% of the homes that sold had 3 bedrooms.

Most homes that sold were built between 2025 and 2026, with a median year built of 2025, so this is mostly newer construction.

Averages hide a lot, so Chris Jenkins compares you to homes that match yours on street, size, age and condition rather than to the whole The Grove median.

sections.h2: Buying in The Grove With Chris Jenkins
sections.html: If you are buying in The Grove, Chris Jenkins sets up a search for the exact streets and price range you want, pulls the recent sales so you know what a fair offer looks like, and negotiates for you. Newer construction can still have builder warranties, so ask what is transferable, and read the association documents closely for dues, rules and any special assessments. Because Virginia sellers give a disclosure statement that tells buyers to do their own due diligence, read our guide to the Virginia Residential Property Disclosure Statement. Confirm flood-zone status and insurance cost for any specific home, since these vary lot by lot.

Figures come from closed residential sales recorded in REIN MLS for Chesapeake between November 15, 2024 and November 14, 2026, grouped under the subdivision name MLS agents use. Medians, not averages, are used so a few very high or low sales do not distort the picture. With 74 sales, this is a solid sample, but every home differs and these figures are not an appraisal or a prediction. Subdivision names in MLS data can cover more than one section of a community.
